text:
Anna K: FYI we saw ~15 soft OOM events on gpu-node-42 during the long-context soak (48k tokens) this morning. Not full process crash, but allocator failed large contiguous allocs and we dropped into degraded path.

Raj P: Can you paste the allocator/profile output?

Anna K: Pasted below — pprof of resident memory + our kvcache slab map. Short summary: total RSS ~78GB, free fragments scattered, largest contiguous free ~1.2GB while we tried to allocate 3.6GB for a merged KV page.

Anna K: ```
pprof: heap_profile
Total: 78_345_120_000 bytes
Top: kv_slab_alloc: 42_000_000_000 bytes
Free ranges: count=12, avg=320MB, max=1.2GB
Attempted alloc: 3_600_000_000 bytes -> ENOMEM fallback -> soft OOM path
```

Mike L: That smells like slab fragmentation from variable chunk lifetimes. Long contexts pin large KV extents, short chats churn small ones. Over time we get holes.

Ciara (eng-runtime): Agreed. In profiling I saw that increasing batch_size from 8->32 increased reuse hits but also increased long-lived extents for batched KV writes, which exacerbates fragmentation.

Raj P: Do we have eviction logs around the events? Any page-in/page-out thrash?

Anna K: Eviction logs show repeated partial evictions, but policy refused to evict some entries marked "pinned_by_inflight". That left many mid-size holes. We also hit mmap fallback because we require contiguous mapping for fast CUDA pinned copy.

oom-bot: [alert] soft_oom_detected node=gpu-node-42 service=kvcache reason=contig_alloc_fail

Mike L: Mitigation ideas: 1) enable on-the-fly compaction (defrag pass) when fragmentation ratio > 0.5; 2) fall back to scattered page map that uses scatter-gather copies (slower) instead of contiguous alloc; 3) lower default contiguous page size for long-context workloads.

Ciara (eng-runtime): I prototyped a compaction pass that merges adjacent free segments and optionally mremap to consolidate. Small test reduced largest free region requirement by ~2x and removed soft OOMs in 10/10 runs. Caveat: compaction causes short CPU spike and stalls requests for ~50-120ms per shard.

Raj P: Could we trigger compaction only during low-latency slack windows (based on P50 queue) or on canary nodes? Or schedule compaction aggressively in Dedicated where customers accept bursty stalls?

Anna K: Another idea: introduce a soft-degrade path where we refuse new long-context requests and return 413/Retry-After when contiguous alloc cannot be satisfied. That avoids falling back to heavy IO. But it's user-visible.

Mike L: We should also tune eviction: allow evicting "pinned_by_inflight" when inflight count > threshold and use safe checkpointing to avoid losing half-completed KV writes. Essentially preemptive eviction.

Ciara (eng-runtime): For immediate hotfix, I deployed a config change to reduce contiguous_page_target from 3.6GB -> 1.5GB and enabled scatter-gather fallback. Patch: ```json
{"kvcache": {"contig_target_bytes": 1610612736, "enable_scatter_fallback": true, "compaction_threshold": 0.6}}
```

Anna K: Hotfix seems to have prevented soft OOMs in the last 3 cycles. Metrics: contig_alloc_fail rate down 95%, kvcache_mmap_fallback up (as expected), request p95 latency up ~40ms for affected paths.

Raj P: Longer term roadmap items:
- Kernel selection: ensure the allocator uses hugepages for large contiguous ranges where possible (reduces fragmentation and speed).
- Batching heuristics: dynamic batch sizing that cap batch length when memory fragmentation high.
- KV reuse: move to multiple fixed-size slab classes (power-of-two) to reduce internal fragmentation.
- Compaction: offload compaction to background threads per-shard with preemption awareness.

Mike L: Also add instrumentation: histograms for contiguous_free_max, fragmentation_ratio (1 - largest_free/total_free), avg_hole_size, compaction_time, scatter_fallback_ratio. These will help auto-trigger mitigations.

Ciara (eng-runtime): I sketched an auto-mitigation policy: if fragmentation_ratio > 0.55 AND contig_alloc_fail_rate > 0.01 over 5m -> reduce contig_target by 2x, enable aggressive compaction, and set batch_size_max = min(current, 8). Revert after 20m of healthy metrics.

Anna K: Sound plan. For release notes we should call out the user-facing change: slightly higher p95 for very long context streams but much fewer soft OOM-caused degraded errors.

Raj P: Who will own the implementation? Ciara -> compaction mechanics + metrics. Mike -> eviction policy + allocator tuning. Anna -> rollout + docs + KB for SREs. I'll PR the auto-mitigation RFC today.

Anna K: Thanks, team. I'll attach the lightweight reproducer in this thread later (small driver that opens many long-lived KV extents with mixed churn). For now keeping the hotfix config pinned on canaries. :thumbsup:

Ciara (eng-runtime): Reproducer posted to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/kv/frag-repro.tar.gz

oom-bot: [info] incident_resolved node=gpu-node-42 service=kvcache duration=2h

Mike L: Follow-up task: consider a memory pool that is GPU-friendly (CUmemPool or ROCm equivalent) to avoid kernel-level fragmentation. I'll investigate next week.

Anna K: OK closing this thread for now. If you see contig_alloc_fail spike on your lanes ping here and we'll escalate.
